primitives.name: Temperature Scaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision Prove that a neural net's overconfident softmax outputs can be fixed post-hoc by dividing logits by a single learned scalar T (chosen to minimize NLL on a validation set) — from "On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks" (arXiv 1706.04599).
primitives.assumptions: Softmax output miscalibration is a uniform scaling across all logits and classes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when calibration error is class-specific or input-dependent.

layer2.mapping: Maps to Bayesian posterior rescaling via logistic loss maximization.
layer2.telemetry: Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on held-out data.

primitives.name: Logistic Posterior Rescaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: The *idea* (one-parameter recalibration as the minimum-viable calibration row) is the right default for signals with tiny held-out samples — a 1-parameter map cannot overfit the way isotonic can — but do not wire this repo's code.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p_{pre} = pre-calibrated probability (unit interval), Δ = shift (log-odds scale)
primitives.assumptions: Pre-existing calibrated logits, linear relationship between prior odds and posterior odds shift.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when prior probabilities are sparse or extreme (near 0 or 1)

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to Temperature Scaling under the logit link function.
layer2.telemetry: Brier score reduction relative to raw model output.

primitives.name: Isotonic Probability Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: The *idea* (one-parameter recalibration as the minimum-viable calibration row) is the right default for signals with tiny held-out samples — a 1-parameter map cannot overfit the way isotonic can — but do not wire this repo's code.
primitives.assumptions: No parametric form assumed, only order preservation; requires sufficient calibration data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfits with small validation sets, leading to piecewise constant approximations.

layer2.mapping: Non-parametric maximum likelihood estimator under stochastic ordering constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Maximum likelihood fit on validation set, cross-entropy loss.

primitives.name: Rank-Based Probability Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The *idea* (one-parameter recalibration as the minimum-viable calibration row) is the right default for signals with tiny held-out samples — a 1-parameter map cannot overfit the way isotonic can — but do not wire this repo's code.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: rank_i = rank of sample i in sorted predicted probability (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Labels are exchangeable given ranks, binning averages approximate conditional expectations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High variance due to coarse binning when sample size per rank bucket is small.

layer2.mapping: Equivalence to histogram binning of scores under empirical distribution.
layer2.telemetry: Histogram-based ECE computed over ranked predictions.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is correcting overconfident neural network outputs that violate proper scoring rules. Temperature Scaling (T=1) assumes uniform overconfidence across all classes and inputs, which is often inadequate. Isotonic Calibration relaxes this homoscedasticity assumption but risks overfitting with limited data. Rank-based methods further simplify by only using the ordering of predictions, discarding magnitude information. All four primitives share the goal of learning a calibration map f(p) ≈ P(Y|p) from a held-out validation set, but differ in their inductive biases: parametric vs. nonparametric, monotonicity vs. shape constraints. In high-stakes applications like sports betting, where calibration errors lead to systematic mispricing, the choice between these methods hinges on the trade-off between expressiveness and robustness to small sample sizes.
